title: Peer scale for the social acceptance of students with special needs: A validity and reliability study.
abstract: This study aimed to develop the Peer Scale for the Social Acceptance of Students with Special Needs (PS-SASSN) and examine its psychometric properties for assessing social acceptance as perceived by typically developing peers in inclusive settings. To establish robust construct validity and prevent overfitting, the study utilized two independent samples of third- and fourth-grade students in Türkiye: the first sample (N₁ = 300) for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), and the second independent sample (N₂ = 300) for Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). Data suitability for EFA was confirmed (KMO = 0.922, Bartlett's test p < .001). EFA revealed a three-factor structure explaining 43.88% of the total variance, comprising "Togetherness and Closeness," "Conflict and Avoidance," and "Help, Protection, and Trust." CFA fully supported this three-factor model, yielding acceptable fit indices (χ/df = 2.78, RMSEA = 0.058, SRMR = 0.065, CFI = 0.921, TLI = 0.914). Reliability analyses indicated high internal consistency, with an overall Cronbach's alpha of 0.936 and subscale coefficients ranging from.823 to.962. The findings provide robust evidence that the PS-SASSN is a valid and reliable multidimensional instrument for assessing peer acceptance in inclusive classrooms, serving as an evidence-based tool for monitoring social interactions and evaluating intervention programs.
